Name: Usage Metering
Desc: A metered-API company's usage platform. API gateways send meter records to the core PostgreSQL database, where ingest stores them as usage events. Billing rates every usage change into its ledger, and finance invoices customers from its copy of that ledger; card payments and refunds live in the payments database. Enterprise customers receive a live copy of their own usage in their own databases, streamed by logical replication from core, and book every row they receive on their usage statements. Support corrects usage (voids, reductions and moves to the right account) with the correction tool, and those corrections must reach every reader. Customers say our numbers disagree. Larkspur and Pell say the live usage copy we stream into their databases still has usage our team voided or moved to another account; Larkspur says a row is in its month-end copy but not its live copy. Several customers say last month's invoice charged usage that was voided. Billing, ingest, the feeds and the invoicing jobs report healthy. Find the root cause. Then make every customer's usage copy match their true usage, including every correction, without disturbing what customers already hold that is correct or booking anything on their statements twice. Make finance's ledger what it would be had it received every ledger change under its own rules, and make sure every customer ends up paying exactly for their true usage across invoices already sent, credits and refunds already given and tonight's routine invoice run, with nothing charged or given back twice. Do not send customers notices or ledger changes for anything that did not change. Keep ingest available. You cannot log into customers' databases.
Supported Operations: Query and change the company's PostgreSQL databases (core, billing, finance, payments, support)
Inspect and run the platform's jobs and their configuration
